data.narrative:
RoboTwin is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Megi Mejdrechová, Ladislav Dvořák, and David Polák, having raised €2.3M in EIC funding. The valuation landscape comprises a comp universe of one public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable to this valuation. While eight same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow peer set. A broad cross-sector median approach would be insufficiently precise given the heterogeneity of robotics subsectors and business models. The single public comparable provides limited leverage for a seed-stage private company analysis.

The absence of sufficient narrow peer multiples means this valuation requires alternative approaches—revenue multiple triangulation, DCF analysis, or venture-standard return-to-exit frameworks—none of which are supported by the data provided. Without either a robust peer median or forward-looking financial projections (revenue, burn, runway), a defensible valuation range cannot be derived from the available inputs. Key uncertainties include the company's current revenue or pre-revenue status, capital efficiency relative to the peer set, and product-market validation stage.
